speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: There will be no other changes to Part 7 of the CTMA, which will continue to enable targeted public health measures to be implemented and adjusted for the purpose of controlling the incidence and transmission of COVID-19, based on the evolving COVID-19 situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: In the past few months, we have taken a three-pronged approach in our response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: Second, we enhanced our healthcare capacity to handle the surges in cases and adjusted our healthcare protocols to right-site care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: For example, lower-risk individuals with mild symptoms can be managed by their primary care doctors, while those at higher risk are assessed for management or monitoring at a care facility or hospital.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: In recent days, we have seen the number of COVID-19 cases peaking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: There are indications that the wave is starting to subside and we are optimistic that with everyone's cooperation in adhering to public health measures, our healthcare system will continue to be able to tend to persons needing care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: However, we must bear in mind that the pandemic is not over yet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: New variants and new waves remain a possibility – it is quite a natural thing that viruses continue to evolve and mutate over time, as we have seen with previous variants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: When such cases and events happen and whether they affect disease transmission and severity, cannot be predicted ahead of time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: New variants can break through borders and we have seen this even in countries with strict zero COVID-19 strategies, resulting in forceful measures having to be implemented, painful ones, like lockdowns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: If Singapore’s re-opening is not carefully managed, infections may rise uncontrollably and potentially overstrain or even cause the collapse of our entire healthcare system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: Even now, our healthcare workers have been labouring, since the pandemic started, for the past two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: SMMs are still needed for now and we will take a gradual and calibrated approach even as we move towards a greater degree of normalcy in our communities, businesses, workplaces and travels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: While we have moved away from lockdowns, which are harmful to the well-being of our people and the economy, we must keep a position where we are nimble and ready to take appropriate measures should the situation worsen or change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: Part 7 of the CTMA ("Part 7"), which allows the Minister for Health to make regulations for the purpose of prevention and control of COVID-19 incidence or transmission, therefore remains relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: As the key legal lever behind various SMMs, Part 7 has served us well by allowing for a multi-faceted public health response to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: It allowed us to weather the Delta and Omicron waves by slowing transmission.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: Group size and safe distancing, for instance, limit the number of interactions persons would have at any point in time, especially in higher risk settings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: This reduces the overall number of interactions a day and therefore limits disease spread.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: Capacity limits are important to prevent overcrowding which can lead to superspreading events.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: In time to come, as case numbers display a sustained and consistent falling trend and the COVID-19 situation abates, we will ease measures along these five key SMMs by adjusting the relevant regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: If COVID-19 ceases to be a threat before the end of this one year, the regulations can be repealed and Part 7 can be allowed to lapse.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister of State for Health)
text: However, if more variants and infection waves take hold, the regulations under Part 7 will continue to be important for the protection of public health.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I will share three perspectives on this Bill.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: First, I would like to propose a more specific modality of extension.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is so that businesses, schools and life in general can go on with minimal disruptions.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While we should remain vigilant against possible new variants, I ask whether there is a need to extend the Bill for another full year.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: What happens next year, if the virus continues to exist and mutate?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: From my conversations with my Yio Chu Kang residents, many dread the thought of continued restrictions on social gatherings, economic activities and events.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: They ask how is this endemic living if we continue to live with these nationwide restrictions that impact social well-being and businesses?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am not suggesting that we do away with the measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: But I hope the Ministry can and will introduce more certainty.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Second, Mr Speaker, Sir , I would like to ask whether the current SMM and VDS measures can be further streamlined.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I am glad to hear from the Senior Minister of State that MOH is intending to do this although the implementation was delayed, given the current Omicron situation.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: An example is the new SMM and VDS measures for coffee shops and canteens.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: The vendors may have more options now, but I have received feedback from the ground about how confusing the new measures are.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Even some young patrons have trouble making sense of them, let alone seniors.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Operators, too, have reported hesitancy to adopt the new measures, given that the added hassle and manpower to ensure compliance.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I believe the abuse that some hawkers received from angry and confused patrons when VDS was first introduced last year remains fresh in their minds.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I have filed a Parliamentary Question on this matter and I look forward to the Ministry's response.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: I also believe that entry into markets and sitting arrangements in hawker centres can be standardised to reduce confusion.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, we should do more to nudge the unvaccinated people to get their shots.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is a general consensus among healthcare professionals and researchers that unvaccinated persons are in danger of severe symptoms and death, which increase the workload for the healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Unvaccinated people also increase the risk of emergence of new variants.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: However, they cannot continue indefinitely as these measures also pose a burden to businesses, institutions and organisations.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We can now leverage on non-mRNA vaccines with high efficacy, like Novavax and oral anti-viral medication, for treatment of patients who are at risk of severe disease.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is continued evidence that our existing public health measures help to reduce transmission even within the same household.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: There is still much we do not know much about COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Studies continue to reveal new possible long-term health complications associated with the virus, such as cognitive decline.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: As we move towards improved vaccines and treatment, avoiding or delaying an infection is important.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We are not yet out of the woods.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: Our healthcare workers continue to struggle with large numbers of COVID-19 cases and they deserve a long overdue break.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While things have definitely been looking up in the past year with the vaccines and boosters, we are still extending and introducing COVID-19 management measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: We need more specific goal posts and simplified measures.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: This is so that the light at the end of the tunnel does not seem out of reach.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Part 7 of the Act concerns the making of control orders by the Minister for Health for the purpose of preventing, protecting against, delaying or otherwise controlling the incidence of transmission of COVID-19 in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Two years on, some other parts of the Act are no longer in force or will expire soon.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: This is a welcome indication that the general direction is to move towards normalcy in our lives and interactions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: On Part 7, the proposal in the Bill to extend its operation by another year appears to be prudent, since COVID-19 is still spreading widely in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, in the months ahead, we do not know whether any variant of concern may emerge.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: It is, therefore, sensible to empower the Minister for Health to issue control measures, if assessed to be necessary to protect public health, including not overwhelming healthcare services.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Nevertheless, looking at where Singapore stands today, it is a matter of time before control measures should be further rolled back or discontinued altogether.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Two years on into the pandemic, we are in a much stronger position on health impacts.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Taking into account cases not officially reported, the percentage of the population who have contracted COVID-19 is probably significantly more.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Further, there are more prevention and treatment options, including a wider range of vaccines, including non-mRNA ones, as well as anti-viral oral drugs to treat COVID-19 patients.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: That said, the fact that COVID-19 is spreading widely through our population, even with such high vaccination rates, should lead us to continue to review whether the control measures we currently have in place remain fit for purpose.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They also add significant cost to businesses and entities which need to implement them and inconvenience members of the public.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Indeed, regular reviews on the efficacy and necessity for any control measures are warranted, so that our people and businesses can return to vibrant economic and social lives as soon as practicable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Members of the House, however, have also sought clarifications on some issues and allow me to take the House through some of them.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked how we can do more to encourage persons who are sceptical of the mRNA vaccines to take up vaccination to protect themselves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As previously highlighted in Parliament, the Novavax Nuvaxovid vaccine has been authorised by the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) and recommended by the expert committee on COVID-19 vaccination for use under our National Vaccination Programme, as an alternative to the mRNA vaccines.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The first batch of Nuvaxovid vaccine is expected to arrive sometime in the months ahead, barring any shipment delays.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This will provide those who may have hesitancy receiving the mRNA vaccine an alternative and I hope they do take this seriously and consider getting themselves vaccinated.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, they do pose a significant load on our healthcare resources and, therefore, VDS is still necessary to protect the unvaccinated and prevent our healthcare system from being overwhelmed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Once the Omicron wave has subsided, we will be in a better position to ease our measures further.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: COVID-19 therapeutics were mentioned by Ms Sylvia Lim and, indeed, they have been authorised by HSA.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But I must explain that they are meant to mitigate the risk of progression to severe illnesses from COVID-19 infection.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Whereas vaccination serves as a more preventive role, that goes further upstream to prevent COVID-19 infection and not allow severe illnesses to take place in the first place.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therapeutics are, therefore, complementary and not substitutes for vaccination.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, we see that the unvaccinated children between zero to 11 years old are at risk of Multi-System Inflammatory Syndrome for Children (MISC), that some Members may have read about in the newspapers as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The incidence in an unvaccinated child can be as high as 470 cases per million infections.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, vaccination is still key to us remaining safe, both on a personal level and at the system level.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng also sought clarification on the rationalisation of SMMs that the MTF recently announced and whether they can be further simplified.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, as explained, this rationalisation is, itself, a way to simplify the SMMs into just five key parameters.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It makes it easier for the public to understand and, in the coming weeks, as we see the cases continue to show a sustained decline, we can then further ease measures along these key parameters.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I note Mr Yip Hon Weng has actually filed a Parliamentary Question on the restrictions at coffee shops and canteens.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I seek the Member's understanding that my colleagues at MSE will look into this and address it at a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked if we might consider a shorter period of extension of Part 7 and base the extension on specific indicators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Ms Sylvia Lim also mentioned that the control measures should be constantly reviewed and make sure that they are fit for purpose.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, we monitor the weekly infection growth rate, the R number, as an indication of virus transmissibility as well as other matrices, like mortality rate, hospital occupancy and our healthcare manpower.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But each variant, as we have seen in the past two years, has somewhat different characteristics and slightly different behaviour, compared to each other and, therefore, no single set of parameters can be solely relied upon and we have to remain nimble and take all factors into account in designing any of these restrictions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As mentioned in my opening speech, we take a calibrated approach in the control measures and have made progressive adjustments to the SMMs as the COVID-19 situation evolves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Members will certainly recall, when the pandemic first started, we actually went into a circuit breaker and, subsequently, a series of Heightened Alert phases, as we cautiously, gradually, tried to reopen social and economic activities to manage the infection risk in our largely unvaccinated population at that time.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: With good progress in our national vaccination efforts towards the end of 2021, our collective resilience and immunity and defence against the virus were strengthened.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, we were able to ride through the wave of Delta infection without resorting to a circuit breaker again and, therefore, we have calibrated some of the measures in dealing with this virus as our own situation evolves.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: When this current Omicron wave hit us, our population had achieved a high vaccination and booster rate, allowing us to then continue on with our progressive reopening and our move towards endemicity, without further tightening of restrictions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Like Members, I, too, hope that we can eventually dispense with the restrictions.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In the opposite scenario, if a variant that can cause more severe illness takes hold, the regulations under Part 7 will continue to be important for the protection of public health.
